papers.title_in_file: Implementing advanced trial wave functions in fermion quantum Monte Carlo via stochastic sampling
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction opening, and Section V Summary and Discussion; methods and result sections skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A classical auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo method that uses stochastically sampled correlated trial wave functions.

assertions.value: The authors state that a large class of correlated wave functions can be implemented as trial wave functions in AFQMC by coupling the random walkers to a generalized Metropolis sampling.
quotes: we demonstrate that a large class of correlated wave functions
can be implemented as trial wave function by coupling the random walkers to a generalized Metropolis sampling
assertions.certainty_reason: Author-reported method demonstrated in their own tests.

assertions.value: The authors state that more sophisticated trial wave functions, such as those with a Jastrow factor, have been challenging to use and their implementation is often assumed to require a quantum computer.
quotes: have been challenging to use and their implementation is often assumed
to require a quantum computer
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's characterization of prior practice, no citation in the abstract.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper offers a classical route to a task often assumed to need a quantum computer.

assertions.value: The authors report that the method yields total ground-state energies systematically within chemical accuracy and preserves the low-polynomial computational scaling of AFQMC, tested on molecules under bond stretching and transition metal diatomics.
quotes: the method yields total ground-state energies systematically within chemical accuracy
preserves the low-polynomial computational scaling of AFQMC
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical results from the authors' own tests on a limited set of molecules.

assertions.value: The authors state that the algorithm as implemented scales proportionally to the number of Metropolis samples, which gives a prefactor to the cost of standard AFQMC with a single determinant trial wave function, and that the implementation has not focused on speedups.
quotes: essentially giving a prefactor to the cost of a standard AFQMC with single determinant trial wave function
our implementation here has not really focused on speedups
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of the cost and scope of the implementation, Section V.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Sections I to III opening, worked examples and closing discussion
papers.what_it_is: A theoretical proposal of quantum neurons whose states are roots of unity, with a neural network built from them.

assertions.value: The paper formulates multiple-valued quantum logic with truth values represented as unique roots of unity on the unit circle, and bases the multi-valued quantum neuron on multiple-valued threshold logic over the complex numbers.
quotes: the truth values are represented naturally as unique roots of unity placed on the unit circle
based on the principles of multiple-valued threshold logic over the field of complex numbers
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition of the construction, Abstract and Section III.

assertions.value: The authors claim that networks built from multi-valued quantum neurons enjoy fast convergence and higher functionalities than quantum neural networks with binary input and the same number of neurons and layers.
quotes: Such neural networks enjoy fast convergence and higher functionalities
compared with quantum neural networks based on binary input with the same number of neurons and layers
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the abstract; the sections read give no training experiment or benchmark.
assertions.reader_inference: No empirical comparison was found in the parts read.

assertions.value: The paper states that, under its qualitative hardware cost model, the minimum cost occurs at radix 3, so using the basis states 0 and 1 plus one superposition state gives a minimum cost.
quotes: the minimum cost happens when r = 3
leads to a minimum cost
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's derivation from a simple cost model that the paper itself calls qualitative.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper itself says its cost model is qualitative.

assertions.value: The author states that the next step is to realize multi-valued quantum neurons experimentally, and that possible practical applications could use quantum neural networks built from orbital angular momentum of light.
quotes: The next step is to realize multi-valued quantum neurons experimentally
Possible practical applications can be found using the quantum neural networks built from orbital angular momentum
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's own statement that experimental realization is still to be done.

papers.title_in_file: Neural Decoders for Universal Quantum Algorithms
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results text on accuracy, loss and timing, discussion and outlook, runtime analysis
papers.what_it_is: A modular attention-based neural decoder for error correction in logical quantum algorithms, evaluated in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that their neural decoders reach logical error rates comparable to most-likely-error decoders across varied circuit depths and qubit counts, and generalize from training on random circuits to unseen multi-qubit algorithmic workloads.
quotes: generalizes from training on random circuits to unseen multi-qubit algorithmic workloads
logical error rates comparable to most-likely-error (MLE) decoders
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation results from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that decoding shot-by-shot yields a time per gate of approximately 27 ms.
quotes: decoding shot-by-shot yields a time per gate of approximately 27 ms
assertions.certainty_reason: Timing benchmark from the authors' own runs on an NVIDIA H100 GPU.
assertions.reader_inference: The batched figure (around 100 microseconds) is in the same sentence but holds a non-ASCII symbol, so it is not quoted.

assertions.value: The authors state that scalability remains an open problem because, as code distance increases, the number of training samples required for reliable performance has been found to grow exponentially, which makes training at large distances prohibitively expensive.
quotes: scalability remains an open problem
the number of training samples required for reliable performance has been found to grow exponentially
assertions.certainty_reason: The exponential growth is attributed to prior work (their ref. 22); the authors state the limit for their own approach.

assertions.value: The authors state that the vast majority of prior machine learning decoder work has focused on quantum memory rather than algorithmic decoding.
quotes: the vast majority of prior work has focused on the conceptually simpler problem of quantum memory
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's characterization of the literature.

papers.title_in_file: Gate teleportation-assisted routing for quantum algorithms
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, benchmark results discussion and conclusions
papers.what_it_is: A qubit routing method that uses gate teleportation through auxiliary qubits to cut circuit depth, tested in compilation benchmarks.

assertions.value: The authors report a depth reduction in the routing of selected algorithms compared to regular routing without using teleported gates.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, p.1 (the numeric range, written with a dash, is not quoted)
quotes: depth reduction in the routing of selected algorithms compared to regular routing without using teleported gates
assertions.certainty_reason: Compilation benchmarks from one study, with assumed teleported-gate times and error rates.

assertions.value: The authors state that their analysis uses values for teleported gates that they expect to be achievable in future devices, and note that current devices exhibit significantly higher error probabilities.
quotes: we chose to use values that we expect to be achievable in future devices
current devices exhibit significantly higher error probabilities
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of the assumptions behind their benchmark, Section 3.1.

assertions.value: The authors state in the conclusions that teleportation-assisted routing can reduce circuit depth by 10 to 20% compared to a native line topology, and that the overhead introduced by auxiliary qubits must be carefully managed.
quotes: teleportation-assisted routing can reduce circuit depth by 10 to 20% compared to a native line topology
The overhead introduced by auxiliary qubits during teleportation must be carefully managed
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result and stated limit; the abstract reports 10 - 25%, the conclusions 10 to 20%.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper states two different ranges (10 - 25% in the abstract, 10 to 20% in the conclusions).

papers.title_in_file: Synergy of machine learning with quantum computing and communication
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section outline and concluding remarks; body sections not read in full
papers.what_it_is: A review of how classical machine learning is applied to quantum computation and communication.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper reviews the classical machine learning models used for quantum error correction, quantum communication, quantum cryptography and mapping quantum algorithms to existing hardware.
quotes: The paper reviews the classical ML models that have been employed in various ways for quantum computation
quantum error correction, quantum communication, quantum cryptography, and mapping quantum algorithms to the existing hardware
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' description of the scope of their own review.

assertions.value: The authors state that the article is not an in-depth review of quantum computation and machine learning but a broad overview.
quotes: This is not an in-depth review of quantum computation and machine learning
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of the review's scope, Section 1.

assertions.value: The authors state that machine learning-enabled quantum computing is a new and fast-growing area in which many challenges remain before it can be at par with classical ML.
quotes: machine learning-enabled quantum computing is a new and fast-growing area, yet many challenges remain before it can be at par with classical ML
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's opinion in the concluding remarks, not a tested result.

papers.title_in_file: TrojanNet: Detecting Trojans in Quantum Circuits using Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, threat model, evaluation results and conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A convolutional neural network that detects Trojan gates inserted into compiled QAOA circuits, evaluated on generated datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report an average accuracy of 98.80% and an average F1-score of 98.53% in detecting and classifying Trojan-inserted QAOA circuits, using 12 generated datasets.
quotes: Experimental results showcase an average accuracy of 98.80% and an average F1-score of 98.53%
we generate 12 diverse datasets
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical results from the authors' own generated datasets in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they assume a user designs a QAOA circuit to solve the Max-Cut problem and employs untrusted or less-trusted third-party compilers.
quotes: We assume that the user designs a QAOA circuit to solve the Max-Cut problem and employs untrusted or less-trusted third-party compilers
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of their own threat model and setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that their Trojan-insertion strategy caused up to a 50% loss in the approximation ratio on benchmark QAOA circuits.
quotes: revealed up to a 50% loss in the approximation ratio
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on benchmark circuits from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that accuracy across the datasets ranges from 97.10% to 100.00%, with an average accuracy of 98.80%.
quotes: ranges from 97.10% to 100.00%, with an average accuracy of 98.80%
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical results from generated datasets (simulated backends), one study.

papers.title_in_file: The Holy Grail of Quantum Artificial Intelligence: Major Challenges in Accelerating the Machine Learning Pipeline
papers.what_it_is: A position paper that deduces four major challenges for quantum artificial intelligence.

assertions.value: The authors deduce four major challenges for the future of quantum artificial intelligence, the last being to build tools that analyze whether observed benefits really stem from quantum properties of the algorithm.
quotes: we deduce four major challenges for the future of quantum artificial intelligence
build tools to thoroughly analyze whether observed benefits really stem from quantum properties of the algorithm
assertions.certainty_reason: Position paper; the challenges are the authors' own analysis, not tested results.

assertions.value: The authors state that none of the surveyed approaches managed to replace large parts of the machine learning pipeline by quantum approaches.
quotes: none of the surveyed approaches managed to replace such large parts of the machine learning pipeline by quantum approaches
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's survey-based statement about the state of the field in 2020.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum AI will only have a success if the quantum part of the algorithm is the part that brings about the advantage.
quotes: QAI will only have a success if the quantum part of the algorithm is the part that brings about the advantage
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's argument in a position paper.
assertions.reader_inference: Relevant to the question of whether a benefit is quantum or only classical.

assertions.value: The authors state that the challenges they define stand without any claim to completeness.
quotes: We defined four major challenges that stand without any claim to completeness
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of scope, Section 6.

papers.title_in_file: Large-scale Efficient Molecule Geometry Optimization with Hybrid Quantum-Classical Computing
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, benchmark results for H4 and H2O2, conclusions
papers.what_it_is: A co-optimization framework combining DMET with VQE to reduce qubit needs for molecular geometry optimization.

assertions.value: The authors report that the DMET plus VQE framework reduced the qubit requirement from 8 qubits to 4 qubits for H4, and from 24 qubits to 18 qubits for H2O2.
quotes: effectively reducing the qubit requirement for the overall H4 simulation from 8 qubits to 4 qubits
the initial qubit requirement of 24 qubits was reduced to 18 qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical results on two benchmark molecules from one study.

assertions.value: The authors claim that their work is the first successful quantum algorithm-based geometry optimization of a molecule of this scale and complexity (glycolic acid).
quotes: the first successful quantum algorithm-based geometry optimization of a molecule of this scale and complexity
assertions.certainty_reason: Priority claim made by the authors, hedged in the text by "to the best of our knowledge".

assertions.value: The authors report that a standard nested loop method demands significantly more iterations and consumes substantially greater computational resources than their framework to achieve convergence on H4.
quotes: the standard nested loop method demands significantly more iterations and consumes substantially greater computational resources to achieve convergence
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical comparison on a small molecule in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that future research will focus on incorporating advanced quantum hardware capabilities and integrating error mitigation and noise-resilient algorithms.
quotes: integrating error mitigation and noise-resilient algorithms to further enhance scalability and reliability
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of work not yet done, Conclusions.
